Subject: OmniWare checkout errors / latency spike - urgent

Hi Camila —

We saw a major spike this morning in error rate and tail latency affecting OmniWare's checkout API (v2). Impact started ~08:50 PDT and has persisted intermittently; conversion dropped by ~18% in the last 30m. Key observations from our side: 

- Error rate (5xx) peaked at 11.4% between 08:50–09:10
- P95 latency from our edge to Redwood increased from ~140ms to ~1.6s
- Throughput was steady but a subset of long sequences (user notes) seems correlated

This is customer-facing and high priority — can you confirm you have a bridge and an estimated ETA for a mitigation? We need an initial readout and an owner for exec updates. I attached a screenshot of our error dashboard.

Subject: Re: OmniWare checkout errors / latency spike - urgent

Camila — I dug into the telemetry in the bridge. Short summary and recommended mitigation: 

Summary of findings (09:20–09:35):
- KV cache eviction rate on the serving tier jumped ~6x correlated with a small set (~2.6%) of requests containing long free-text notes; these requests increased average token length and caused higher KV memory churn.
- The runtime's continuous batching pulled some of those long requests into large batches causing temporary GPU memory pressure and request timeouts (5xx) while the kernel retried.
- There are no obvious network errors at the infra layer; the failure mode appears to be runtime memory pressure + batch compaction.

Immediate mitigation (I can run now if you approve):
A) Reduce max batch size on the affected pool from 64 -> 32 and enable aggressive KV-preserve policy for the next 45 minutes. This reduces throughput slightly but eliminates batch compaction spikes.
B) Route 20% of traffic to quantized variant model-q4 for a 30-minute canary to protect user experience while we adjust cache sizing.

Estimated rollout timeline: 10 minutes to push batch/caching flags + 5 minutes for traffic split, monitor 30 minutes. If stable, we revert to gradual ramp over 2–4 hours with improved cache thresholds.

I recommend we push A+B immediately. Ellen — expected customer-visible improvement within ~10–15 minutes after flags applied.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin

Ellen — quick exec readout and commitments (internal + customer-facing):

What happened (brief): A sudden percent of long-sequence requests increased KV cache churn, which in combination with continuous batching produced transient GPU memory pressure that led to request retries and elevated 5xx rates. Networking and infra checks are negative.

Immediate actions taken (completed):
- Applied batch size limit change and KV-preserve flags to the affected serving pool (10:12 PDT).
- Deployed 20% traffic to model-q4 quantized variant as a safeguard (10:17 PDT).
- Monitoring dashboards and alerts tightened; we will stream token-level traces to the OmniWare team for verification.

Commitments and timeline:
- 0–30m: Stabilize throughput and confirm reduction of 5xx to <0.5% (in progress).
- 30m–4h: Gradual ramp of batch size back to baseline with revised cache thresholds; validate analytics and run synthetic load.
- 24–72h: Post-incident root-cause analysis (RCA) delivery with concrete config changes, test plan, and regression guardrails.

Customer compensation proposal: 1 month service credit for the impacted checkout traffic window — pending approval from Sales Ops.

Attachments: commitment_sheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48KB); postmortem-outline.md (text/markdown, 6KB)

Please confirm this plan and whether you'd like a formal exec readout briefing with Redwood leadership later today. Marcus — thanks for moving fast.
